newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says he hopes to sign Hebron deal on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says he hopes to sign Hebron deal on Tuesday.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said he hoped to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later on Tuesday to sign a deal on a long-awaited Israeli troop pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Arafat spoke after meeting U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who arrived late on Monday to press the two sides for swift agreement on a Hebron withdrawal accord.
Asked if he would meet Netanyahu later in the day to sign an accord, Arafat told reporters: "We hope so. If everything goes smoothly we can have this opportunity."

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have held marathon sessions to nail down final details of an agreement on a troop withdrawal from 80 percent of Hebron, the West Bank flashpoint from which the Jewish state should have pulled back last March.
Arafat said of the negotiators: "They are working through issues that are complex and in very great detail. They are working hard."
He declined to go into details, but said that talks would continue on Tuesday morning.
